facing_notes: OpenRA facings are WAngle units: 1024 per full turn, 0 = north (screen up), increasing COUNTER-clockwise (WVec.Yaw = ArcTan(-Y, X) - 256, so west = 256, south = 512, east = 768; WAngle.FromFacing(f) = f * 4 for the classic 0..255 facing, FromDegrees(d) = d * 1024 / 360). For a sequence with Facings N (N a power of two <= 1024) the facing block is chosen by OpenRA.Mods.Common.Util.IndexFacing: step = 1024 // N; block = ((angle + step // 2) & 1023) // step. If the sequence has UseClassicFacings (RA 32-facing vehicle/turret art, ClassicSpriteSequence) the block comes from OpenRA.Mods.Cnc.Util.ClassicIndexFacing instead: with SpriteRanges = [20, 56, 88, 132, 156, 184, 212, 240, 268, 296, 324, 352, 384, 416, 452, 488, 532, 568, 604, 644, 668, 696, 724, 752, 780, 808, 836, 864, 896, 928, 964, 1000] the block is the first i with angle < SpriteRanges[i], else 0 (so angles 1000..1023 and 0..19 use frame 0; frame 1 covers 20..55, frame 2 covers 56..87, ...). The actual facing drawn by classic block i is SpriteFacings[i] = [0, 40, 74, 112, 146, 172, 200, 228, 256, 284, 312, 340, 370, 402, 436, 472, 512, 552, 588, 626, 658, 684, 712, 740, 768, 796, 824, 852, 882, 914, 948, 984]. A negative Facings in yaml means reverse_facings: block = (N - block) % N. With InterpolatedFacings M > N the closest block is drawn rotated by GetInterpolatedFacingRotation = (AngleDiffToStep(angle, N) // (1024 // M)) * (1024 // M) where AngleDiffToStep = ((angle + step/2) & 1023) % step - step/2 (none of the images here use it). Sprite index inside the sequence (DefaultSpriteSequence.GetSprite): index = block * length + (frame % length). That index addresses the 'frame_table' of each sequence, which this file has already resolved per DefaultSpriteSequence.CalculateFrameIndices: for block b and animation frame i, i_virtual = (i * facings + b) if transpose else (b * stride + i); sheet index = start + i_virtual, where the sheet is the file's frames, or the explicit Frames list when the yaml gives one (ResolveSprites expands Frames first, so source frame = Frames[start + i_virtual]; Length: * then means len(Frames) - start); stride defaults to length. Reverses appends the inner frames in reverse order (length becomes 2*length-2). If shadow_start >= 0 the shadow frame for a source frame f is f - start + shadow_start. For a plain sequence the frame_table ints are frame indices of 'file' (PNG '<file>-NNNN.png'); for a Combine sequence they index the 'combine' list, whose entries name the real file and frame.
frame_addressing_notes: Each sequence carries: file (shp/tem stem; PNG name is '<file>-<frame:04d>.png'), start, length, stride, facings, reverse_facings, tick (ms per frame), offset [x, y, z] in pixels added to the sprite position, z_offset (WDist units, 1024 per cell; higher draws on top), z_ramp, shadow_start, shadow_z_offset, flip_x, flip_y, transpose, reverses, classic_facings (UseClassicFacings), frames (explicit Frames list or null), scale, alpha, alpha_fade, blend_mode, ignore_world_tint, combine (virtual sheet for Combine sequences or null) and frame_table (list indexed [facing_block][frame]).
wall_notes: brik/sbag idle, scratched-idle and damaged-idle have 16 frames with no facings: WithWallSpriteBody plays frame = adjacency bitmask where bit 1 = same wall type to the south (dy > 0), bit 2 = west (dx < 0), bit 4 = north (dy < 0), bit 8 = east (dx > 0).
bib_notes: WithBuildingBib draws the 'bib' sequence of the building image as a strip of tiles under the footprint: rows = 1 if HasMinibib else 2, width = Building.Dimensions.X, and bib frame i goes to cell (i % width, i // width + Dimensions.Y - rows) relative to the building's top-left cell. fact/weap use bib2 (3 wide), powr/barr/hpad use bib3 (2 wide), gun/agun/sam/ftur use their own 1-row mbXXX minibib. Building sprites are centred on the centre of the Dimensions rectangle plus LocalCenterOffset (BuildingInfo.CenterOffset).
